atom: An implementation of an object is linearizable if, for any complete concurrent execution of the object, there is a sequential execution with the same operations and return values whose total order of operations is a linearization of the partial order of operations in the concurrent execution.

question: Some track structure codes use ionization and excitation cross sections obtained for gas-phase atoms when simulating water. For which interactions are these cross sections in principle unsuitable, and why?
key:

In addition, gas-phase data cannot capture the solid/liquid effects on ionization thresholds and the subsequent ion-molecule/hydrogen-bond-mediated relaxation, so they are only approximate for water.
